report.source_text: The results revealed two compound heterozygous variants at NM_017651.4: c.2105C>T (p.T702M) (Fig. 2A) and c.1330A>T (p.I444F) (Fig. 2A) in the AHI1 gene. The c.2105C>T variant was inherited from the unaffected mother, and the c.1330A>T variant was inherited from the unaffected father (Fig. 1A). According to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines [10], both the c.2105C>T and the c.1330A>T mutations were predicted to be of uncertain significance. However, c.2105C>T has been previously reported as pathogenic (rs756276537) in the compound heterozygous pattern with c.903_910insAp.T304fs*309 [11] or alongside another pathogenic variant (p.E281*) [12]. On the other hand, c.1330A>T mutation has not been reported in the popular public databases, but its pathogenicity could be predicted by Mutation Taster, SIFT and PolyPhen-2. The CADD phred score was 28.2.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Joubert syndrome with ocular defects (JS-O) caused by compound heterozygous variants in the AHI1 gene
clinician.trajectory_summary: 31-year-old Chinese Han male with a 29-year history of progressive visual impairment beginning with night blindness in early childhood. At age 5 years, he was diagnosed with macular degeneration based on fundoscopic findings. Over the subsequent 24 years, he received vitamin B12, B1, and B6 supplementation with stable visual acuity but progressive visual field narrowing. At age 29 years, he developed intention tremors and gait imbalance over a 2-year period. On admission, ophthalmologic examination revealed tubular visual field, retinal pigmentation on fundus photography, and retinal nerve fiber layer thinning on OCT consistent with retinal dystrophy. Neurological examination documented intention tremor on finger-nose pointing, gait instability on toe-heel and straight walking, slight bilateral nystagmus, and decreased smooth pursuit, with normal muscle strength and tone. Brain MRI demonstrated a molar tooth sign in the midbrain and cauda cerebelli hypoplasia, pathognomonic findings for Joubert syndrome. Genetic testing identified compound heterozygous variants in the AHI1 gene: c.2105C>T (p.T702M) inherited from the unaffected mother and c.1330A>T (p.I444F) inherited from the unaffected father. The c.2105C>T variant has been previously reported as pathogenic in compound heterozygous patterns, and c.1330A>T is predicted to be pathogenic by multiple in silico tools (Mutation Taster, SIFT, PolyPhen-2) with a CADD phred score of 28.2. The diagnosis of Joubert syndrome with ocular defects (JS-O) was confirmed by the combination of clinical presentation, characteristic brain MRI findings, and genetic confirmation.
